rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For every community God prescribed a manāsik, meaning worship, its place, or a sacrificial offering.
rows.anchor: أي عبادة أو موضع عبادة أو قربانا

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Sacrificing ritual offerings and shedding blood in God's name remained prescribed across all religious communities.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن كثير : ولم يزل ذبح المناسك وإراقة الدماء على اسم الله مشروعا في جميع الملل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose of prescribing these rites is that people remember God's name over their sacrifices, offerings, and worship, in gratitude for His provision of livestock.
rows.anchor: على ذبائحهم وقرابينهم وعبادتهم كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because one God instituted all true laws, He alone deserves worship; branches of revealed law may differ and some may abrogate others.
rows.anchor: وإن اختلفت فروع شرائعه ونسخ بعضها بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers must submit outwardly and inwardly to every command and prohibition, whether abrogating or abrogated, even when a rite's meaning is not understood.
rows.anchor: انقادوا بجميع ظواهركم وبواطنكم في كل ما أمر به أو نهى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhbitīn are humble and broken-hearted; the word derives from khabt, low ground fit for passage and other benefits.
rows.anchor: أي المتواضعين , المنكسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humble tremble in fear when God is mentioned, patiently endure every affliction, and steadfastly maintain prayer despite pilgrimage's hardships.
rows.anchor: والصابرين } الذين صار الصبر عادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They continually spend what God provides, including costly offerings, because they recognize His blessing and trust in His replacement of what they give.
rows.anchor: على الاستمرار , بالهدايا التي يغالون في أثمانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels are singled out for their great size and esteem, or because Arabs alone among earlier peoples were distinguished by them.
rows.anchor: الإبل أعظمها خلقا , وأجلها في أنفسهم أمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Camels are among God's ritual signs; ishʿār marks an offering camel by piercing its hump with a blade to distinguish it from other camels.
rows.anchor: بحديدة في سنامها , تمييزا لما يكون منها هديا عن غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camels benefit people in this world through subjection and in the next through drawing near to God by offering them.
rows.anchor: بالتسخير الذي هو من منافع الدنيا , والتقريب الذي هو من منافع الآخرة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Aisha reports that on the Day of Sacrifice no deed is dearer to God than offering an animal; its horns, hooves, and hair come on Resurrection Day, and its blood reaches God before the earth, so sacrifice gladly. Al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan.
rows.anchor: روى الترميذي وحسنه وابن ماجة عن عائشة رضي الله عنها أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Daraqutni reports Ibn Abbas quoting the Prophet that the best expenditure of silver is an Eid-day sacrificial offering.
rows.anchor: ما أنفقت الورق في شيء أفضل من نحيرة في يوم عيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The camels are to stand for sacrifice with their left forelegs tied; God's magnification through obedience makes their slaughter permissible despite their greater size and strength.
rows.anchor: صواف } قياما معقلة الأيدي اليسرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their sides falling means they have cooled as their souls depart and stopped moving.
rows.anchor: أي سقطت سقوطا بردت به بزوال أرواحها فلا حركة لها أصلا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir cites a marfūʿ report instructing people not to hasten the soul's departure.
rows.anchor: في حديث مرفوع ) ولا تعجلوا النفس أن تزهق (

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Al-Thawri transmits in his Jāmiʿ through Ayyub, Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, and Farafisa al-Hanafi Umar's version of the instruction not to hasten the soul's departure.
rows.anchor: عن فرافصة الحنفي عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may eat from a voluntary offering if one wishes; eating does not make it cease to be an offering to God.
rows.anchor: إذا كانت تطوعا إن شئتم الأكل , فإن ذلك لا يخرجها عن كونها قربانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's first definition is that al-qāniʿ humbly approaches to ask, while al-muʿtarr is the asker.
rows.anchor: أي المتعرض للسؤال بخضوع وانكسار { والمعتر } أي السائل

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi reverses the definitions: al-qāniʿ is the asker, while al-muʿtarr is a visitor or passerby.
rows.anchor: وهو قول الشافعي رحمه الله , قال في كتاب اختلاف الحديثك والقانع هو السائل

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says the root q-n-ʿ conveys turning toward something: the asker turns toward the person asked, and the contented person toward what satisfies him.
rows.anchor: وأصله في اللغة أن القاف والنون والعين تدل على الإقبال على الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The astonishing subjection of powerful camels should prompt reflection and gratitude, expressed by obeying the rules for what may be forbidden, allowed, and offered.
rows.anchor: أي لتتأملوا ذلك فتعرفوا أنه ما قادها لكم إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God receives neither sacrificial meat nor blood; what reaches Him is taqwā, the heart's quality that guards against divine anger and motivates obedience.
rows.anchor: أي عمل القلب وهي الصفة المقصود بها أن تقي صاحبها سخط الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People once splashed sacrificial blood on the House and placed meat around it, wrongly treating this as devotion; the verse abrogates those outward customs and makes inner purpose decisive.
rows.anchor: وكانوا ينضحون البيت ونحوه بدماء قرابينهم

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi takes the verse as evidence that sincere intention is better than prescribed deeds.
rows.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن النية الخالصة خير من الأعمال الموظفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples had also rejected messengers as mere humans; Pharaoh's mission came after a long interval, signaled by then.
rows.anchor: وطأن الرسالة إليهم كانت بعد فترة طويلة , فدل عليها بحرف التراخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's people were the most affluent and powerful of their age, had many forces, and enslaved the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: وكانوا أترف أهل زمانهم , وأعظمهم قوة , وأكثرهم عدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron were supported by miracles and a clear binding proof: God's protection and elevation of Moses over powerful opponents unable to thwart him.
rows.anchor: وهي حراسته وهو وحده , وأعلاه على كل من ناواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's people arrogantly refused the call without reflection; their description as an established people of superiority indicates their corrupt nature and strength over peers.
rows.anchor: إلى أنهم أوجدوا الكبر عن الاتباع فيما دعوا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They rejected the messengers because they were human like themselves and because their peoples were enslaved to Pharaoh's court, which they treated as proof of superiority.
rows.anchor: والحال أن قومهما { لنا عابدون * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's counterargument is that people plainly differ greatly in knowledge and ability; if such differences are possible, humanity alone cannot disqualify a messenger.
rows.anchor: لما جعلوا هذا شبهة لم يجعوا عجزهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his chiefs denied Moses and Aaron, so God drowned them all; their power and enslavement of Israel could not avail them, while Israel's weakness did not harm them.
rows.anchor: بإغراقنا كلهم على تكذيبهم إشارة إلى أنهم لم يهلكوا بأنفسهم من غير مهلك مختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns those who accuse chaste, heedless believing women: their chastity keeps them from evil, their heedlessness from even mentioning it, and their faith restrains wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أي اللائي جعلن أنفسهن نم العفة في مثل الحصن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such accusers are cursed in this world and the next and face immense punishment; passive wording stresses the curse and its broad occurrence rather than naming its agent.
rows.anchor: أي أبعدوا عن رحمة الله , وفعل معهم فعل المبعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The belief qualifier matters: accusing a nonbelieving woman is forbidden but does not carry this same combined judgment; the passage chiefly honors the chaste believer Aisha.
rows.anchor: وقيد بوصف الإيمان لأن قذف الكافرة وإن كان محرما ليس فيه هذا المجموع

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says the Mothers of the Believers, especially Aisha as the occasion of revelation, fall under the warning; he reports consensus that post-revelation slander of her is unbelief and calls inclusion of the remaining Mothers the sounder of two views.
rows.anchor: قال ابن كثير : وأمهات المؤمنين أولى بالدخول في هذا من كل محصنة لا سيما التي كانت سبب النزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day their tongues, hands, and feet will testify to slander and all other deeds, exposing denials when they think lying may help.
rows.anchor: وأيديهم وأرجلهم } إن أنكرت ألسنتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day God will repay them fully with the just recompense they deserve, beyond anyone's ability to challenge.
rows.anchor: أي جزاءهم { الحق } أي الذي يظهر لكل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With causes and veils removed, they will know that God alone is the manifest truth and regret their worldly neglect of vigilance.
rows.anchor: الثابت أمره فلا أمر لأحد سواه , { المبين * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole surah's treatment of the incident of the Slander is the Qur'an's strongest condemnation of any sin, honoring the Messenger and protecting his household.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى ما غلظ في شيء من المعاصي ما غلظ في قصة الإفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heaven will split greatly with clouds, like earth splitting to send forth plants; omission of the tāʾ hints that the event may be hidden to some.
rows.anchor: خفاء على البعض - بما أشار إليه حذف تائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels will descend gradually by an irresistible command, not all at once as the disbelievers had demanded.
rows.anchor: بأمر حتم لا يمكنهم التخلف عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes the seven heavens splitting in succession; each higher heaven has more inhabitants than the one below, followed by the cherubim and bearers of the Throne.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : تشقق السماء في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day true sovereignty belongs to the All-Merciful alone; every other ruler retains only a name and no actual authority.
rows.anchor: ومعنى التركيب أن ملك غيره في ذلك اليوم إنما هو بالاسم الذي تقدم له في تسميته به فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His mercy means His allies rejoice at the punishment of those who opposed them for abandoning truth, and no one would enter Paradise without His mercy.
rows.anchor: ومن عمم رحمته وحقية ملكه أن يسر قلوب أهل ورده بتعذيب أهل عداوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day is especially and severely difficult for disbelievers, whose denial of it will bring profound regret.
rows.anchor: أي فقط { عسيرا * } شديد العسر والاستعار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer bites both hands in extreme regret at that day's terrors, having turned from the noblest guide to the good and kept company with one leading to evil.
rows.anchor: ويوم يعض الظالم } أي لفرط تأسفه لما يرى فيه من الأهوال { على يديه } أي كلتيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking one's desire as a god means devoting oneself to worshipping desire, leaving no path to righteousness; reversing the word order would make desire subordinate to God instead.
rows.anchor: ولو قيل : من اتخذ هواه إلهه , لكان المعنى أنه قصر هواه على الإله

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan explains the verse to mean that the man has taken no god except his desire.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : والمعنى أنه لم يتخذ إلها إلا هواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Word order changes meaning: making a servant one's father elevates the servant, whereas making one's father a servant demeans him; similarly, the verse's order makes desire the sole object of worship.
rows.anchor: فلان اتخذ عبده أباه , لكان معناه أنه عظم العبد , ولو قيل : إنه اتخذ اباه عبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet cannot act as a divinely appointed guardian who compels a person away from desire; he is responsible only for conveying the message, so he should not grieve himself over them.
rows.anchor: لست بوكيل , ولكنك رسول , ليس عليك إلا البلاغ , فلا تذهب نفسك عليهم حسرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question denies that most addressees hear or reason in a way that benefits them and might lead them to return voluntarily.
rows.anchor: أي هؤلاء المدعوين { يسمعون } أي سماع من ينزجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble cattle in failing to use reason and are even more astray: unlike cattle, they do not heed warnings, thank benefactors, avoid enemies, desire reward, or fear punishment.
rows.anchor: بل هم أضل } اي منها { سبيلا * } لأنهم لا ينزجرون بما يسمعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their misguidance veils reason; if they believed, the veils would lift and faith would illuminate their sight of subtle meanings and hidden realities.
rows.anchor: بظلال الجبال الشامخة من ضلالهم , ولو آمنوا لانقشعت تلك الحجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as physical sight cannot distinguish visible things without sunlight, the intellect's spiritual insight cannot grasp meanings as they are without faith's light; spiritual insight is the soul's eye, as sight is the body's.
rows.anchor: الإنسان - وإن كان بصيرا - لا يميز بين المحسوسات ما لم يشرق عليها نور الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's work in the inward realm illuminates it with the sun of spiritual knowledge just as He works in the outward world, showing how He deprives them of benefit from what He gave them.
rows.anchor: ولأن عمله في الباطن ينيره إذا شاء بشمس المعارف كعمله في الظاهر سواء , دليلا على سلبهمالنفع بما أعطاهموه
